# Winterizing the hive

## Timing

Everything done by the first week of October, before the ivy flow finishes and the bees get tetchy. 2024 jobs done on 5 October, a mild dry Saturday, 14°C. Colin Prowse came round to help lift, and in return I held the ladder while he did his gutters, see [[Gutter cleaning]].

## Stores and hefting

Each hive needs about 20 kg of stores to get through a Devon winter, which is mild but long and wet.

### Feeding in September

Heavy syrup, 2 parts sugar to 1 part water by weight, in Ashforth feeders. 2024 totals:

- Primrose: 9 kg sugar
- Bramble: 7 kg
- Hazel: 11 kg (after the mite trouble, see [[Varroa mite treatment]])
- Ivy: 12 kg, a first-year hive with almost nothing put by

Feeders off by 28 September.

### Hefting

Lift the back of the hive an inch with one hand and feel the weight. Better: the luggage scale (Salter, £9) hooked under the back, then the front, add the two. October 2024 readings: Primrose 43 kg, Bramble 38 kg, Hazel 40 kg, Ivy 31 kg. Hefted again every 3 weeks through the winter.

### Fondant

A 2.5 kg block of Ambrosia fondant, cut in half, over the feed hole on Ivy from 15 January 2025, and on Bramble from 9 February. Ivy ate the lot by March.

## Mouse guards

Metal strips with 9.5 mm holes pinned across the entrance on 5 October, after the first cold night. A mouse got into Bramble in winter 2022 and chewed out four frames. Never again.

## Insulation and ventilation

### Roof

50 mm of foil-backed insulation board cut to fit inside the roof of each hive, offcuts from Colin's loft. Warm roof, so condensation forms on the walls and runs down, instead of dripping onto the bees from above.

### Floor

Open mesh floors left open, varroa boards out except during counts. Ventilation from below keeps them dry. A damp hive kills more bees than a cold one.

## Weather proofing

- Hives strapped down with ratchet straps after the Storm Ciarán gales of November 2023 tipped Primrose's roof into the brambles
- Hive stands checked level, a slight tilt forward so rain runs out of the entrance
- Chicken wire cages round all four from 1 December against green woodpeckers; one drilled straight through Hazel's brood box in February 2023

## Winter treatment

Oxalic vapour in late December when broodless, all written up in [[Oxalic acid vapour dosing]]. Done 28 December 2024.

## The quiet months

I visit once a week just to look at the entrance, clear dead bees off the landing board with a bent wire, and listen with an ear to the side. A low hum is good. Silence means a heft and maybe a peek. Spring 2025: all four alive, Ivy the smallest, Primrose roaring by 1 April.
